correctness.rationale: Top-quota selection gives capture fraction 2^-i for any admissible tail; its union with a fixed earlier set remains admissible. Block masses vanish for finite-norm vectors, since a geometric subsequence of heavy blocks would make anchored-one norm infinite. Every higher-anchor secondary chain fits unchanged into an anchored-one chain, so K_i <= blockmass_i + K_1 and each vector has a finite fixed norming anchor. Combining its arbitrary-accuracy norming sets with capture yields coordinatewise norm rigidity. Truncation and finite-seminorm arguments yield FIN=EXH and equinormed compactness. Uniform-counting on two blocks proves failure of all stated directedness classes. At most one block from [N,2N) lies in any admissible set, giving exact isometries and norm-one projections. The standalone finite verifier passes and is never used to justify infinite quantification.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper obtains equinormed compactness from positive uniform directedness and presents a non-l1 example satisfying (0,1/9). Our particular family has norm rigidity and equinormed compactness while failing every (lambda,gamma) class with lambda<1/2 and gamma>0; therefore those published positive implications cannot cover it. Its isometrically 1-complemented l_infty^N blocks and the coordinatewise norm-rigidity implication form a motivated new conjunction not found in the inspected 2024 general theory. Published-index and own-claim comparison revealed no implication; search cannot establish uniqueness beyond inspected sources.
residual_risks: Nonindexed or differently named Banach lattice/Kadec--Klee results or a combinatorially equivalent family might exist.

value.rationale: Addresses an explicit recent gap in the strength of directedness assumptions for compactness of combinatorial sequence sets: a norm-rigid, equinormed-compact example provably lies beyond every positive uniform near-directedness hypothesis. Arbitrarily large 1-complemented isometric l_infty blocks demonstrate a non-l1 geometry, so the phenomenon cannot be attributed merely to the classic ell_1 norm. This new structural boundary is motivated and not an arbitrary finite slice; it does not require a complete classification or solve the separate open (0,0)-approach case.
